paper.title: Giant transposable elements drive genetic diversification in Aspergillus oryzae, a domesticated fungus traditionally used in food fermentation
paper.authors: Hamanaka Y, Katayama T, Chiken Y, Nishiguchi K, Yamaguchi K, Shigenobu S, Maruyama JI.
paper.association_evidence: Data availability: 'The RNA-seq data of A. oryzae strains is available as the DDBJ BioProject PRJDB37768 and PRJDB42568'; key resources table lists PRJDB42568 as RNA-seq of A. oryzae strains in PD agar medium.

study_summary.objective: Map the giant Starship transposable elements of A. oryzae, compare them with A. flavus, and ask how their cargo genes contribute to strain diversification during domestication.
study_summary.experimental_design: Genomes of five industrial TK strains were sequenced and compared with RIB40; RNA-seq of RIB40, TK-35 and TK-41 grown on PD agar over cellophane at 30 C for 2 days (one library per strain) tested whether Starship cargo genes are expressed.
study_summary.main_finding: Cargo genes inside Starship elements are transcribed and not silenced relative to genes elsewhere in the genome, so they may remain functional.
